name: Hyundai (Hyundai Motor America)
verdict: Hyundai Motor Company is listed and family-controlled; South Korea's National Pension Service holds about 7.8%.
note: Rating note: on hold. The state link doesn't count: South Korea's National Pension Service holds about 7.8% of Hyundai Motor (hyundai-owner-record), and South Korea has no record in this data (re-rated from concern on 2026-09-27, docs/rating-review-2026-09-27.md). The company test isn't settled. A US Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division investigation found that a 13-year-old worked 50 to 60 hours a week on an assembly line at SMART Alabama, a Hyundai subsidiary, in 2021-22; on 30 May 2024 the department sued Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama, SMART Alabama and a staffing firm in the US District Court for the Middle District of Alabama (AP in Alabama Daily News, 2024-05-31, https://aldailynews.com/us-labor-department-sues-hyundai-suppliers-over-alleged-child-employment/; CBS News, 2024-05-30, https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hyundai-alabama-child-labor-act-labor-deparment/). Korea Daily reported on 2025-11-14 that the court had found Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama 'could be held liable as a joint employer' (https://en.koreadaily.com/hyundai-kia-labor-lawsuit/); no final judgment was found. Held as not rated yet until that case ends (maintainer decision, 2026-09-30): if it ends with a finding against Hyundai, the rating is set from it and a record claim is written; if not, this sponsor is `none`. No record claim is written yet.
